about: r9-12 / r8-25 / r4D-5 — ONE name per address in every place it is named (headers, the switcher, Activity, Settings, sheets, invites; this device's own accounts too). The rule is the link door's `names.label {address, own, kept, registered}`: `registered` (the passkey index's name — the account's own published name, the same answer on every device) first, then `kept` (what a multisig on this device keeps for it), then `own` (this device's local account name — a fallback only), then the short EIP-55 address. Every shell draws the accounts machine's `member_labels[lowercase address]`, which is this rule over what the device knows; a shell never picks a name itself. Replay each case through the door and compare the answer.

cases.name: the phones' account: the index's published name, never the local fixture name (r10 'Interleave' vs 'Parallel One')
the published name before a label an invite carried
no index name: the kept label (an invite's, or the name typed when the member was added)
this device's own account the index does not hold yet: its local name
a blank name is no name
